cases.explain: «отдельной комнате» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The Brothers Make Friends Ivan was not, however, in a separate room, but only in a place shut off by a screen, so that it was unseen by other people in the room. It was the first room from the entrance with a buffet along the wall. Waiters were continually darting to and fro in it. The only customer in the room was an old retired military man drinking tea in a corner. But there was the usual bustle going on in the other rooms of the tavern; there were shouts for the waiters, the sound of popping corks, the click of billiard balls, the drone of the organ. Alyosha knew that Ivan did not usually visit this tavern and disliked taverns in general. So he must have come here, he reflected, simply to meet Dmitri by arrangement. Yet Dmitri was not there.

cases.sentence: — Я все помню, Алеша, я помню тебя до одиннадцати лет, мне был тогда ___.
cases.explain: «пятнадцатый год» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I remember everything, Alyosha, I remember you till you were eleven, I was nearly fifteen. There’s such a difference between fifteen and eleven that brothers are never companions at those ages. I don’t know whether I was fond of you even. When I went away to Moscow for the first few years I never thought of you at all. Then, when you came to Moscow yourself, we only met once somewhere, I believe. And now I’ve been here more than three months, and so far we have scarcely said a word to each other. Tomorrow I am going away, and I was just thinking as I sat here how I could see you to say goodbye and just then you passed.”

cases.sentence: Я видел, как ты на меня смотрел все эти три месяца, в глазах твоих было какое-то ___, а вот этого-то я и не терплю, оттого и не подошел к тебе.
cases.explain: «беспрерывное ожидание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Very. I want to get to know you once for all, and I want you to know me. And then to say goodbye. I believe it’s always best to get to know people just before leaving them. I’ve noticed how you’ve been looking at me these three months. There has been a continual look of expectation in your eyes, and I can’t endure that. That’s how it is I’ve kept away from you. But in the end I have learned to respect you. The little man stands firm, I thought. Though I am laughing, I am serious. You do stand firm, don’t you? I like people who are firm like that whatever it is they stand by, even if they are such little fellows as you. Your expectant eyes ceased to annoy me, I grew fond of them in the end, those expectant eyes. You seem to love me for some reason, Alyosha?”

cases.sentence: Ты и теперь для меня загадка, но нечто я уже осмыслил в тебе, и всего только с ___!
cases.explain: «сегодняшнего утра» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I do love you, Ivan. Dmitri says of you—Ivan is a tomb! I say of you, Ivan is a riddle. You are a riddle to me even now. But I understand something in you, and I did not understand it till this morning.”

cases.sentence: — А ты в ___ так скоро уезжаешь, брат?
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “But are you really going so soon, brother?”

cases.sentence: Да, пожалуй, и не догадается она никогда, несмотря даже на ___.
cases.explain: «сегодняшний урок» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Alyosha,” laughed Ivan, “don’t make reflections about love, it’s unseemly for you. How you rushed into the discussion this morning! I’ve forgotten to kiss you for it. … But how she tormented me! It certainly was sitting by a ‘laceration.’ Ah, she knew how I loved her! She loved me and not Dmitri,” Ivan insisted gayly. “Her feeling for Dmitri was simply a self-laceration. All I told her just now was perfectly true, but the worst of it is, it may take her fifteen or twenty years to find out that she doesn’t care for Dmitri, and loves me whom she torments, and perhaps she may never find it out at all, in spite of her lesson today. Well, it’s better so; I can simply go away for good. By the way, how is she now? What happened after I departed?”
